executiveSummary: GM0214 passes the deterministic contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its CBS 2025 identity, generalized boundary, 27,978 residents, 39 neighbourhoods, 16 BAG places, 35 BRT settlements, eight physically identified road corridors, absence of a ProRail station and 48 transit stop areas are coherent. Nulls, zero-intensity behavior, local reconciliation, causal ledgers, cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours and map-layer invariance also pass. Release remains correction-required. The simulator gives river, pluvial and heat all 39 neighbourhoods in exactly the same rank order even though Buren's published heat plan names built-up cores and its municipal sewer/terrain model provides separate T10/T100/T1000 water footprints. That public model counts 126 measured-floor buildings with water ingress at T100, whereas the simulator emits one unsupported municipal flood-depth-like value and a common hash. A focused ignition inside an official TOP10NL deciduous-forest polygon leaves the source neighbourhood twelfth rather than controlling direct flame. The canonical river preset holds a precise 2.140015 m-labelled screening value and zero recovery through T+72 without a selected defence/breach, depth, arrival or recession surface; Buren has genuine river and seepage risk, so the conservative state is Unknown rather than zero or safe. Two public sewer pumps whose source status is 'niet meer aanwezig' are rendered indistinguishably from realized assets. Public water, provider, antenna, school, government and transit records remain context only. Complete physical utility topology, operating state, backup, stocks, crews and restoration commitments are unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented; all utility transfers remain logical road-derived proxies.

evidenceSources.title: Lokale Adaptatie Strategie 2022, Uitvoeringsplan Klimaatadaptatie and Lokaal hitteplan 2022–2025
evidenceSources.edition: LAS adopted 2022; execution programme 2023–2027; local heat plan 2022–2025
supports: The official LAS distinguishes drought, heat, short and prolonged heavy rainfall, river seepage and flooding. It identifies river seepage particularly in northern Buren and Zoelen; structural water nuisance at Brinkstraat in Lienden; other reported locations in Lienden, Eck en Wiel and Ingen; and risk at bedrijventerrein 't Hulster in Buren.

The municipality reports low general soil storage dependent on groundwater, with locally higher stream ridges. Its 2021 integrated sewer-and-surface model used T10/T100/T1000 design storms and estimated roughly 60–135 homes could receive water for T10/T100. The companion execution plan https://www.buren.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Uitvoeringsplan-Klimaatadaptatie-Deel-1-2022.pdf reports about 125 residential-use buildings with modeled ingress at T100 and says floor levels, reports and practice knowledge were used.

The LAS names Maurik, Lienden, Buren, Zoelmond, Beusichem and Eck en Wiel as strongly paved heat attention areas, with Lienden the most paved. The local heat plan https://www.buren.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Lokaal-hitteplan-gemeente-Buren-website-versie.pdf names the same cores and supplies separate apparent-temperature and distance-to-cool-place maps; these are planning evidence, not a T+0 observation or a numerical health-effect function.

These adopted PDFs are municipality-wide qualitative/model documentation with no machine API, explicit blanket redistribution licence or fixed refresh cadence. Their observed reports, long-term climate context and design events must remain distinct from the synthetic 72-hour clock.

evidenceSources.title: Buren Hoosbuientest public map configuration, WMS and WFS
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal 2021 sewer/surface stress-test layers; public configuration inspected 2 September 2026
supports: The public machine configuration exposes municipality-scale T10/T100/T1000 water-depth classes and building-outcome classes. WMS access is https://mapserver.viewer-duopp.nl?map=/etc/mapserver/duopp_buren.map&SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities&VERSION=1.3.0 and WFS access is https://mapserver.viewer-duopp.nl?map=/etc/mapserver/duopp_buren.map&SERVICE=WFS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities&VERSION=2.0.0 in EPSG:28992; vector output is GML and advertised shapefile rather than GeoJSON.

Reproducible WFS resultType=hits counts by T10/T100/T1000 are red measured-floor ingress 55/126/188, orange measured-floor lower-than-road without computed ingress 15/43/35, gray computed water but floor unmeasured 117/384/1,637, green measured-floor no ingress 462/363/309 and white floor not measured 14,497/14,230/12,977. The T100 red count corroborates the published approximately 125 buildings.

White and gray classes are unresolved floor-level semantics, not zero hazard or safety. Design-event layers are modeled scenario evidence, not current rainfall, current inundation, annual observed losses or a forecast.

The public configuration and capabilities state no blanket reuse licence or guaranteed refresh cadence. Before redistribution or causal use, the municipality/publisher must confirm licence, model edition, storm hyetograph, terrain/sewer versions, units, uncertainty and whether detailed sewer layers are suitable for public operational display.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Beleidsplan 2024–2027 with Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024 context
supports: The official four-year strategic plan explicitly includes Buren among the 14 municipalities and its risk diagram includes flooding from high river water, heatwave, nature fire near vulnerable objects, electricity, telecom/ICT and gas disruption, drinking-water contamination and road/rail/shipping hazardous-material incidents.

It explains increasing electricity-system pressure and digital dependency, and identifies drier/hotter conditions, heavy rainfall and nature fire near vulnerable objects as continuing regional concerns. It emphasizes cross-boundary partner networks for complex and prolonged crises.

This is formally adopted qualitative regional context, not a municipal hazard footprint, live incident feed, probability/depth field, asset inventory, service-state observation, staffing count or restoration promise. It is a PDF with a statutory four-year policy cycle and no stated machine API or blanket reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: Public ArcGIS REST water-system, groundwater, drainage-area and primary-defence services
evidenceSources.edition: Live ArcGIS REST directory inspected 2 September 2026; primary-defence reporting layer 2025
supports: The public machine directory exposes JSON/GeoJSON/PBF-capable Feature/MapServer layers for watercourses, controls, groundwater/infiltration, drainage areas and water defences. Useful endpoints include https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Waterkwantiteit/Gebieden_oppervlaktewater/MapServer, https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Watersysteem/Legger_en_Werkingsgebieden_Wateren_Vastgesteld/MapServer and https://portal.wsrl.nl/kaarten/rest/services/Veiligheidsrapportage_Primaire_kering_2025/MapServer.

The drainage-area service contains locally named contexts including Aalsdijk en Buren, Beusichem, Eck en Wiel and Linge Tiel-Buren. These areas, watercourses, controls and defences are more physically relevant than a municipality-centre river distance but do not by themselves establish a selected breach, exceedance, water level, connection, control state, depth, arrival or recession.

The service covers the Waterschap Rivierenland management area at object/catchment scale. The inspected metadata does not state a single blanket public reuse licence or guaranteed cadence across services; each selected layer needs its item metadata, source/measurement date, update policy, units and licence retained.

evidenceSources.title: Landelijk Informatiesysteem Water en Overstromingen
supports: LIWO provides professional map layers for Dutch water nuisance and flooding and is the integration candidate for named depth, arrival and hydraulic-event footprints after an expert selects a physically connected Buren scenario.

IPLO explicitly warns that correct interpretation requires specialist water-manager knowledge. LIWO content cannot be converted from missing coverage to zero, combined indiscriminately across defence/breach events, or presented as a current forecast.

The public web/download product is release-versioned rather than advertised on a fixed operational cadence. No blanket machine API, reuse licence or resolution applies to every layer on the landing page; retain per-layer terms, scenario, probability class, resolution, units, NoData and release notes.

evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public-context snapshots and live APIs inspected 2 September 2026
supports: HWH Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are national OGC APIs under CC BY-SA 4.0. Kunstwerken is published weekly while DAMO contribution cadence/completeness varies. The current GM0214 polygon intersects 537 display-only points: 17 sewer pumps, 28 surface-water pumps, two sluices and 490 weirs. Connectivity, units, control state, capacity, emergency power and live function remain unknown.

Two DAMO sewer-pump records, RG Eck en Wiel at [5.45368268676471, 51.97352272512617] and RG Lienden at [5.517647301769031, 51.94876694919548], explicitly have status 'niet meer aanwezig'; 535 other intersecting points have status 'gerealiseerd'. Historical/withdrawn objects must not be rendered as current without a distinct status style.

Public-domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows identifies Liander for electricity (feature updated 24 March 2026) and gas (17 December 2025), Vitens for water and Ziggo for fixed media (both 7 September 2025) at the municipality reference point. Provider areas identify connection responsibility, not topology, capacity, quality, outage or restoration.

The deployed boundary snapshot also contains 43 RDI antenna registrations, 19 DUO education records and six KVK government-service records, while the RIVM acute-care intersection is empty. RDI coverage/cadence and reuse terms require source review; DUO RIO is national daily around 06:15 under CC BY; KVK OGC is partial Public Domain; RIVM questionnaire releases are versioned CC0 context. Presence or absence is never live capacity or availability.

KNMI Data Platform https://dataplatform.knmi.nl supplies national CC BY 4.0 Open Data/EDR/notification APIs, including near-real-time 10-minute observations and product-specific forecasts/grids. Valid time, issue time, station/grid coverage, uncertainty and product cadence must accompany any weather input; this can replace fictional meteorology only when the scenario explicitly selects observed or forecast mode.

findings.summary: One hazard-independent neighbourhood hash makes Buren river, pluvial and heat maps exactly rank-identical despite distinct official local evidence.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3577-3591 uses one hazardSeed based on city seed, scenario seed and region id. All 39 river/pluvial/heat ranks match exactly, led by Verspreide huizen Rijswijk, Verspreide huizen Ravenswaaij and Verspreide huizen Maurik. E03 instead identifies Lienden, Maurik, Buren, Zoelmond, Beusichem and Eck en Wiel as built-up heat attention areas; they rank 33, 31, 30/27, 26, 34 and 38. E04 supplies a separate municipal sewer/terrain pluvial model. The documents and design layers are not observations or zonal means, but prove that the simulator order is not source-derived.
findings.action: Until event-specific geometry is integrated, mark neighbourhood ranks unsupported and prohibit dispatch, evacuation or resource priority from them. Make the local multiplier hazard/event specific; use polygon-aware aggregation with source edition, event/reference date, units, native resolution, licence, uncertainty and NoData retained.

findings.summary: An integration-ready municipal T10/T100/T1000 pluvial model is ignored while the simulator presents one unsupported Buren flood-depth-like value.
findings.evidence: At canonical pluvial T+24 the simulator reports floodDepthM 0.360964, severity 0.260696, drainage availability 0.483846, 2,927 affected people and 97,578 cumulative proxy person-hours. E03-E04 document a 2021 integrated sewer/surface model with measured floor levels and expose WMS/WFS depth/building classes. WFS resultType=hits returns 126 red measured-floor ingress buildings at T100, corroborating the published approximately 125; it also returns 384 gray possible-ingress/unmeasured-floor and 14,230 white unmeasured-floor buildings. The canonical 0.360964 is not tied to any of these events, pixels, building classes, drainage states or observed rainfall.
findings.action: Smallest safe correction: label the current pluvial number synthetic and make neighbourhood depth/priority Unknown. After municipality licence/model-definition clearance, ingest only the public hazard/building-result classes for a named T10/T100/T1000 exercise, preserve gray/white as Unknown, and keep detailed sewer topology non-causal unless explicitly authorized. Validate against published counts and event metadata.

findings.summary: An explicit ignition inside official deciduous forest does not control the displayed Buren local wildfire impact.
findings.evidence: E02 identifies TOP10NL forest object 106231486 and focused source [5.444801850736001, 51.93125639622181] inside BU02140206 Verspreide huizen ten oosten van kanaal. A focused synthetic T+24 run reports direct fire 0.470474, smoke 0.414102, drought 0.476580 and city severity 0.459933, yet the source neighbourhood ranks twelfth at 0.506113 while Verspreide huizen Rijswijk ranks first at 0.538355. Static forest cover and this diagnostic are neither an observed incident nor a forecast, but they falsify source-aware local allocation.
findings.action: Keep direct-fire neighbourhood ranks visibly synthetic/unsupported and prohibit operational rank use. Make local allocation source/perimeter and eligible-fuel aware using versioned TOP10NL as an open CC BY 4.0 static fallback, while modeling transported smoke, drought, valid-time KNMI weather, access, extinguishing water and suppression assumptions separately.

findings.summary: A coarse major-river proximity field presents precise persistent Buren inundation without a selected local hydraulic event.
findings.evidence: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-471 uses municipality-reference-point distance to approximate national river segments. At T+24 and T+72 the canonical river preset reports floodDepthM 2.140015, severity 0.666246 and zero service recovery; affected population is 19,649 then 20,318 and cumulative event-attributable person-hours 253,441 then 1,016,361. E03 confirms genuine flooding and northern/Zoelen river-seepage concerns, E06 provides water-board catchments/defences and E07 provides event layers, but no selected connected defence/breach/control state, depth, arrival, duration or recession surface supports the displayed municipality-wide amplitude. This is not evidence that Buren is flood-safe.
findings.action: Conservatively render direct GM0214 river impact Unknown/numerically neutral until an expert selects a named, connected and versioned LIWO/Waterschap event. Keep river defence, seepage, local drainage/pluvial and indirect access/supply pathways separately visible and unresolved; never convert unavailable event coverage to zero or safety.

findings.summary: Two sewer pumps explicitly marked 'niet meer aanwezig' are rendered like current realized water assets.
findings.evidence: E08 and the deployed water-assets snapshot contain 537 points in GM0214. RG Eck en Wiel and RG Lienden have source status 'niet meer aanwezig', while 535 records have status 'gerealiseerd'. apps/web/src/components/MapView.tsx:616-624 loads all points into one clustered source and :1630-1695 filters only on cluster state and assetType; no operational-status filter or style is applied. The inspector correctly says public register context rather than live state, but identical symbols can still imply that withdrawn pumps exist now.
findings.action: Before release, retain source history but exclude withdrawn records from default current-asset counts or style them explicitly as historical/withdrawn. residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Buren disaster, outage, casualty, evacuation, welfare or restoration dataset.
The 2025 generalized CBS boundary is appropriate for municipal aggregation but not parcel-level hydraulics, asset ownership, response jurisdiction or exact incident geometry.
Buren's hoosbui layers are modeled design-event outputs, not observations; detailed sewer layers require explicit reuse/licence, model-edition and security review before redistribution or causal use.

Official river, seepage, defence, watercourse and asset context does not prove hydraulic connection, failure, depth, arrival, duration or recession; a water-management expert must select and version a physically relevant event.
TOP10NL forest cover is static context rather than live fuel, moisture, spread, suppression or access state; the focused BU02140206 ignition is synthetic.
HWH/provider/antenna/facility/GTFS records are partial dated context, not complete topology, capacity, operating state, backup, stock or restoration commitments.
No reviewed public safe source supplies complete Liander, Vitens, municipal sewer, gas, telecom, care, food/fuel or emergency-resource topology/state; sensitive detail was not inferred.

First-72-hour household behavior, medically dependent people, responders, mutual aid, shelters, pharmacies, fuel/food stocks, crew travel, repair priorities and visitor/daytime demand remain scenario assumptions or Unknown.
